# Selectors

How a step names the element it acts on. A bare string is a CSS selector; the forms below are the explicit spellings.

## `CssSelector`

Explicit CSS selector.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `css` | `str` | `required` |


## `XpathSelector`

Explicit XPath selector.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xpath` | `str` | `required` |


## `IdSelector`

Shorthand for [id="..."] attribute selector.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | `required` |


## `RefSelector`

A selector named symbolically; the run's selector map supplies it.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `str` | `required` |


## `FallbackSelector`

Try primary selector first, fall back if no match found.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | `CssSelector \| XpathSelector \| IdSelector \| FallbackSelector` | `required` |
| `fallback` | `CssSelector \| XpathSelector \| IdSelector \| FallbackSelector` | `required` |


## `ScopedSelector`

`inner`, looked for inside the `index`-th match of `root`.

What a step's `in: <as>` builds, once per pass: the root is re-resolved
and re-indexed every time, so no handle outlives the pass that made it.

| field | type | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `str \| CssSelector \| XpathSelector \| IdSelector \| FallbackSelector` | `required` |
| `index` | `int` | `required` |
| `inner` | `str \| CssSelector \| XpathSelector \| IdSelector \| FallbackSelector` | `required` |
